name: Kenrith's Transformation
oracle_text:
Enchant creature
When this Aura enters, draw a card.
Enchanted creature loses all abilities and is a green Elk creature with base power and toughness 3/3. (It loses all other card types and creature types.)
blocked_sentences: Enchanted creature loses all abilities and is a green Elk creature with base power and toughness 3/3. (It loses all other card types and creature types.)

needs.what: a static effect (layer 4) that REPLACES a permanent's creature types with a printed list for as long as it applies -- here `affects: {"attached": true}` making the enchanted creature's creature subtypes exactly ["Elk"] (a Human Wizard loses Human and Wizard) -- e.g. `subtypes` on the `set_types` static, or a `set_subtypes` static, read in `characteristics` beside layer 0. The same need as goddric_cloaked_reveler's gap.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `set_types: ["Creature"]` with `affects: {attached: true}` removes the other card types (Artifact) but keeps every subtype whose class is still present (characteristics.py layer 0 keeps creature subtypes because Creature remains), and the loader refuses `set_types` with empty `types`, so the subtypes cannot be wiped and rebuilt with `add_subtype` either; `add_subtype` ["Elk"] only unions, giving a Human Wizard Elk that a Human lord still pumps. The `animate` op's `exact` flag does replace creature types, but it is a one-shot op whose duration is only until_end_of_turn or permanent, so it would outlive the Aura. Everything else is expressible: card-level target `enchanted` (Creature), a self_enters `draw` trigger, and attached statics `lose_all_abilities`, `set_colors` ["G"], `set_types` ["Creature"], `add_subtype` ["Elk"], `set_pt` 3/3 -- so only the creature-type replacement is missing and no partial answer was written.
